analysis:
Examined the docs/provider/troubleshooting.md changes (date bump, a reworded `usage reporting` row at head line 87, and a new `Requests served` row at head line 144) plus the one-line addition to ProviderLoop+Trust.swift (head ~lines 69-70), which adds `cancellationsPartialComplete: stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` to the DaemonState.Stats snapshot.

Docs: the changes are explanatory only. They introduce no new commands, endpoints or trust claims. The new row correctly states that the local status count may exceed paid Earnings and includes cancelled or dropped requests and self-route requests. It does not overclaim attestation or runtime secrecy, so it is consistent with T-056 and T-058. The `usage reporting` reword narrows the semantics and does not weaken any control.

Swift: the change adds one integer counter to the local `~/.darkbloom/daemon-state.json` snapshot, which is written by the owner-only local path and read by `status` and `doctor`. The counter holds no prompt content, keys or identifiers. Nothing in the visible patch sends it to the coordinator, so A-001 is not exposed. It touches no authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage path (T-041 and T-053 are untouched).

Open integration questions, not findings: (1) the definition of `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` and the DaemonState.Stats field/Codable decoding live in unchanged or unsupplied files, so I could not verify they exist and that decoding stays backward compatible with older state files. This is a build/compat concern, not a security one. (2) Whether the counter is later surfaced in reports (`darkbloom report`) or heartbeats was not visible. The counter itself is low sensitivity (timing and activity metadata only).

No security regressions identified in the supplied units.
